parent_objective: design a fair self-ID go/no-go controller matrix after the source-diverse pressure hard stop
blocked_by: source-diverse pressure replay positives remain source-singleton and control-sensitive
supersedes: another source-diverse pressure replay loop without controller-family go/no-go comparison

public_gates: M1492 must design the L0/L1/L2/L3 fair controller matrix before new training or replay
M1492 must preserve the deployable human-view/no-privileged actor input contract
M1492 must pre-register shared budgets, seeds, task families, metrics, and falsification criteria
M1492 must block private holdout tuning, promotion, corpus export, PPO, and actor-input changes
forbidden_shortcuts: do not claim recurrent self-identification from M1490 source-singleton positives
do not compare controller families with different budgets or tuning recipes

workflow_synthesis.evidence_increment: turns the M1491 source-diverse pressure hard stop into a fair L0/L1/L2/L3 controller-family design
workflow_synthesis.claim_scope: design only; no replay run, training, PPO, promotion, private holdout, corpus export, paper-level or level3 self-identification claim
stop_condition: stop if the matrix gives one family a larger budget, different seed set, or extra actor inputs
stop if finite-window and GRU controllers are not separated from capacity controls
stop if private holdout is used for tuning
stop if design attempts to promote a checkpoint
fallback_plan: if the matrix cannot be made fair with current tooling, add a small infrastructure design milestone for missing loaders or config validators
if current-sim task families are underspecified, first write task-family manifests without training
workflow_synthesis.synthesis_trigger: new branch opened after M1491 hard stop

admission_evidence: M1491 applies the M1488 hard stop because M1490 positives remain source-singleton and control-sensitive
docs/self-id-go-no-go-paper-route-plan.md defines L0/L1/L2/L3 controller families and task families
allowed_updates: status queue scoreboard research log and review
one follow-up implementation or manifest route for the matrix
next_stage_criteria: fairness and falsification criteria are pre-registered
next implementation or experiment route is explicit

self_id_evidence_discipline.current_frame_substitution_risk: M1492 is a design milestone whose purpose is to test whether current-frame response, finite-window history, or recurrent hidden state actually explains behavior.
history_necessity_tests: pre-register L0-current, L1-one-step, L2-finite-window, L2-current-tiled, L3-online-GRU, and L3-reset/truncated controls
pre-register wrong, delayed, removed, and truncated history interventions as evaluation criteria rather than assumptions
self_id_evidence_discipline.temporal_evidence_window: design only; no new temporal evidence generated.
self_id_evidence_discipline.negative_result_policy: If current-response or finite-window controllers match GRU under fair budgets, treat recurrent self-ID as negative or conditional instead of weakening the claim standard.
allowed_claims: M1492 designs a fair self-ID go/no-go matrix
no promotion, corpus export, training, PPO, private-holdout, paper-level result or level3 self-identification claim

hypothesis: The correct next step after the source-diverse pressure hard stop is a fair L0/L1/L2/L3 controller-family go/no-go matrix, not another replay retargeting loop.
success_criteria: design defines L0-current L1-one-step L2-finite-window L2-current-tiled L3-online-GRU and L3-reset/truncated controllers
design defines T1 through T5 decisive task families
design pre-registers shared budgets seeds metrics and falsification criteria
design blocks training PPO replay promotion private holdout corpus export and actor-input changes
failure_criteria: controller families have unequal budgets or hidden extra inputs
finite-window and GRU capacity controls are omitted
design uses private holdout for tuning
design starts training replay PPO promotion corpus export or actor-input change
decision_rule: M1492 passes if it registers a fair controller-family go/no-go design before any new training or replay.
